canonical_data: application-defined agent memory and workforce task state
current_repo_note: Paper-associated and maintained by a research collective, but with a real release train, a large test suite, and continuous integration, so it passes the test that excluded paper harnesses. Framework-primary is a defensible alternative reading; the flagship module, name, and description are the multi-agent society. A separate commercial product is built on it by the same organisation.
strengths: A full orchestration runtime with pause, snapshot, and resume rather than a prompt pattern
Failure handling that creates new workers at runtime is implemented and tested
Provider and sandbox breadth without any vendor lock, including local runtimes and container execution
weaknesses: The release train stalled at pre-release alphas for five months while commits continued
Two files of over six thousand lines each hold the orchestrator and the chat agent, making audit costly
Research-collective governance with a separate commercial product sitting on top
why_it_matters: The oldest surviving role-playing multi-agent framework, now carrying a production-style workforce orchestrator alongside its research heritage.
